travelGuide.title: Hargeisa Travel Guide
travelGuide.subtitle: Practical information to help you plan a smooth trip
travelGuide.visaBody: Most nationalities can obtain a Somaliland visa on arrival at Egal International Airport (HGA), or in advance from a Somaliland representative office abroad. Bring two passport photos and pay the fee in USD.
travelGuide.airportBody: Egal International Airport (HGA) sits about 5 km from the city center. Taxis and hotel shuttles are available outside arrivals; agree on a fare before departing.
travelGuide.transportBody: Shared and private taxis are the main way to get around the city. Ride-hailing apps are limited, so hotels can arrange trusted drivers for day trips and airport transfers.
travelGuide.currencyBody: The Somaliland shilling (SLSH) is the local currency, though US dollars are widely accepted for hotels, larger purchases and taxis. Mobile money (Zaad, eDahab) is used everywhere, even in small shops.
travelGuide.safetyBody: Hargeisa is generally safe for visitors who take normal precautions. Dress modestly, avoid photographing government or military buildings, and check locally for the latest security guidance before travel.
travelGuide.emergencyBody: Police: 999 · Hargeisa Group Hospital: available via hotel front desk · Always keep your hotel's address and phone number with you.
travelGuide.internetBody: Local SIM cards (Telesom, Somtel) are inexpensive and easy to buy with a passport. Data coverage is solid in the city center; most hotels and cafes also offer WiFi.
travelGuide.customsBody: Somaliland is a conservative Muslim society. Dress modestly, greet with your right hand, and expect Friday to be a rest day for many businesses.
travelGuide.bestTimeBody: November to February offers the coolest, most comfortable weather. The rainy season (April–May) can make travel outside the city harder.
travelGuide.packingBody: Light, modest clothing (long sleeves and trousers/long skirts recommended), a scarf for women, comfortable walking shoes, sun protection, and a universal power adapter.
travelGuide.faq1Q: Do I need a visa to visit Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq1A: Most travelers can get a Somaliland visa on arrival at the airport, though it's worth checking current requirements for your nationality before you fly.
travelGuide.faq2A: Hargeisa is considered one of the more stable and welcoming cities in the region, but as with any destination, it's wise to stay informed and use common-sense precautions.
travelGuide.faq3Q: What language is spoken in Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq3A: Somali is the primary language, with Arabic and English also widely understood, especially in hotels and among younger residents.

transportation.title: Transportation
transportation.subtitle: How to move around Hargeisa comfortably and safely
transportation.airportTransfersBody: Egal International Airport (HGA) is roughly 5 km from downtown. Most hotels can arrange a pickup; airport taxis are also readily available.
transportation.taxisBody: The most common way to get around. Agree on the fare before you get in, or ask your hotel to book a trusted driver.
transportation.minibusesBody: Shared minibuses run fixed routes across the city and are the cheapest option, though schedules are informal.
transportation.rentalBody: Self-drive rentals are uncommon; most visitors hire a car with a driver for day trips outside the city, arranged through hotels or tour operators.
